strategies.name: Naive Looped All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Direct translation of reference: 8 iterations, each with one all_reduce followed by local forward coupling, backward decoupling, and buffer preparation. 8 all_reduce dispatches total. Simplest structure but highest dispatch overhead; no fusion or overlap attempted.

strategies.name: Pipelined Reduce-Scatter All-Gather Chain
strategies.desc: Replace each all_reduce with reduce_scatter (producing W shards) followed by all_gather to reconstruct full vector. Each rank computes local coupling/decoupling only on its owned shard during the RS phase, broadcasts via AG. 16 dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but enables per-rank parallelism in coupling computation and potentially smaller per-dispatch payload during RS phase.

strategies.name: Fused Local-Op Batching
strategies.desc: Precompute all 8 stages' coupling/decoupling coefficient matrices, then perform all_reduce calls with staging buffers that allow fusion of multiple local operations between dispatches. Still 8 all_reduce calls but local loops are vectorized/fused across stages where dependencies allow, reducing host-device synchronization overhead.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc: Exploit multi-node topology (if num_nodes > 1): perform intra-node all_reduce (across cores_per_device * num_devices per node), apply coupling transformations on node-aggregated results, then inter-node all_reduce, final broadcast. Reduces cross-node bandwidth by factor of (world_size/num_nodes) at cost of additional intra-node dispatches; approximately 8*(2+1) = 24 dispatches for two-level hierarchy.

strategies.name: Overlapped Computation with Async Collectives
strategies.desc:
Issue all_reduce asynchronously and overlap coupling computation for independent shards (rank r coupling uses shard r+1, so shards 0 to W-2 have dependencies but last shard is independent). Pipeline stage k's all_reduce with stage k-1's local decoupling via careful buffer rotation. 8 all_reduce dispatches but wall-time reduced through compute-communication overlap.
